record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Given an infinite-dimensional system that satisfies the local input-to-state stability estimate with comparison functions β and γ, determine or estimate the actual region in the product space of states and inputs on which that LISS estimate is valid. In particular, go beyond existence proofs and obtain usable bounds for the validity region in X × U.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.26. The proof of Theorem 2.25 is based on converse Lyapunov theorems for the 0-UAS property, see [161], and thus it does not give a precise estimate for the region in X ×U for which the LISS estimate (1.6) is valid (for given β, γ). The estimation of the region in which the LISS estimate is valid is a hard problem, which has not been touched so far for infinite-dimensional systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(X,\|\cdot\|_X)$ be a Banach space (the state space) and $(U,\|\cdot\|_U)$ a normed space of admissible input values; let $\mathcal{U}$ be a normed space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to U$ (e.g. $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},U)$) endowed with norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{U}}$. Consider a forward complete control system $\Sigma$ on $X$ with input space $\mathcal{U}$, whose solution starting from $x\in X$ under input $u\in\mathcal{U}$ is denoted $\phi(t,x,u)$, defined for all $t\ge 0$ on the relevant domain.

Recall that a function $\gamma:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is of class $\mathcal{K}$ if it is continuous, strictly increasing, and $\gamma(0)=0$; it is of class $\mathcal{K}_\infty$ if additionally $\gamma(r)\to\infty$ as $r\to\infty$. A function $\beta:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\times\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is of class $\mathcal{KL}$ if $\beta(\cdot,t)\in\mathcal{K}$ for each fixed $t\ge 0$ and $\beta(r,t)\downarrow 0$ as $t\to\infty$ for each fixed $r\ge 0$.

The system $\Sigma$ is called locally input-to-state stable (LISS) if there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$, $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$, and constants $\rho_x,\rho_u>0$ such that for all $x\in X$ with $\|x\|_X\le \rho_x$ and all $u\in\mathcal{U}$ with $\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}\le \rho_u$, the trajectory $\phi(\cdot,x,u)$ exists for all $t\ge 0$ and satisfies
$$\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X \;\le\; \beta(\|x\|_X,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}), \qquad t\ge 0. \tag{$\ast$}$$

More generally, given $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$, define the validity region
$$R(\beta,\gamma)\;:=\;\bigl\{(x,u)\in X\times\mathcal{U} : \phi(\cdot,x,u)\text{ is global and }(\ast)\text{ holds for all }t\ge 0\bigr\}.$$

Problem. Develop a method that, beyond merely asserting the existence of some neighborhood of $(0,0)\in X\times\mathcal{U}$ contained in $R(\beta,\gamma)$, yields explicit, usable lower bounds on $R(\beta,\gamma)$ for a given LISS infinite-dimensional system $\Sigma$ and given comparison functions $\beta,\gamma$. In particular, produce constructive estimates (for instance via Lyapunov-type or other functional-analytic techniques) of the largest sublevel-style set $\{(x,u)\in X\times\mathcal{U} : \|x\|_X\le r_x,\ \|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}\le r_u\}\subset R(\beta,\gamma)$, and more generally describe quantitatively the shape of $R(\beta,\gamma)$ in $X\times\mathcal{U}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of obtaining usable bounds on the validity region of a LISS estimate for infinite-dimensional systems appears to remain open. The authoritative survey on ISS for infinite-dimensional systems explicitly lists this as untouched, and recent related work (e.g., 2024–2025 papers on local integral ISS for non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems and on estimating ISS gain functions via finite-dimensional approximations) addresses related but distinct questions, without providing general constructive estimates of the LISS validity region in $X\times\mathcal{U}$.

status_evidence.snippet: Estimation of the region in which the LISS estimate is valid is a hard problem, which has not been touched so far for infinite-dimensional systems.

status_evidence.title: Estimation of the input-to-state stability gain functions from finite-dimensional approximations
status_evidence.snippet: Estimation of ISS gain functions via finite-dimensional approximations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on estimating gain functions, not on bounding the LISS validity region in X×U.

status_evidence.title: Local integral input-to-state stability for non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Local integral ISS for non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works address local ISS variants but do not provide general usable bounds on the LISS validity region.
